title: Refund Basis, Full Refund Window and Proration Rounding for Circle Members
content:
## Refund terms recorded for your Northbeam Circle Membership tier

Each tier of Northbeam Circle Membership records how dues are refunded on cancellation, the days from
activation within which dues are refunded in full, and how a prorated amount is rounded.

| Tier | Refund basis recorded | Full refund window (days) | Proration rounding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Circle Free Membership | no dues to refund | 0 | not applicable |
| Circle Plus Annual | full refund inside the early window, then nothing | 14 | whole unused months, USD to 2 decimal places |
| Circle Total Annual | full refund inside the early window, then prorated by whole unused months | 30 | whole unused months, USD to 2 decimal places |
| Circle Total Household Annual | full refund inside the early window, then prorated by whole unused months | 30 | whole unused months, USD to 2 decimal places |
| Circle Business Pro | prorated by whole unused months | 0 | whole unused months, USD to 2 decimal places |
| Circle Business Elite | prorated by whole unused months | 0 | whole unused months, USD to 2 decimal places |

## How the three entries read together

On Circle Plus Annual the recorded basis is a full refund inside the early window and nothing after it,
and that window runs 14 days. On Circle Total Annual and Circle Total Household Annual the basis is a
full refund inside the early window and a proration by whole unused months after it, over a window of 30
days. On Circle Business Pro and Circle Business Elite the basis is a proration by whole unused months
and the full refund window is recorded as 0 days. On Circle Free Membership there are no dues to refund
and the window is recorded as 0 days.

Rounding is recorded identically on the five tiers that can produce a prorated figure: whole unused
months, with the money taken to 2 decimal places. On Circle Free Membership the rounding entry is
recorded as not applicable.
